# Copilot Instructions

- **Purpose**: This package is a Tailwind CSS plugin that adds production-ready UI states for the Premium AI Headshots preview experience (loading, image reveal, errors, upsell, badges) with built-in dark-mode overrides.
- **Entry points**: [index.js](../index.js) re-exports the plugin defined in [tailwind-ai-preview-plugin.js](../tailwind-ai-preview-plugin.js). There is also a duplicate export shim at [.github/index.js](index.js); keep these in sync if the entry filename changes.
- **Plugin structure**: All component classes live in [tailwind-ai-preview-plugin.js](../tailwind-ai-preview-plugin.js) using Tailwind’s `plugin()` helper and `addComponents`. Light theme styles are defined inline; dark theme overrides are grouped in a single `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` block near the bottom.
- **Core classes**: Loading (`.fade-in`, `.preview-loading`, `.progress`, `.progress-bar`), skeleton placeholder (`.skeleton` uses direct `height`/`width` plus `@apply`), image wrapper (`.preview-image-container`, `.preview-image.loaded`), overlays (`.preview-overlay button`), error UI (`.error-state`, buttons/icons), upsell (`.upsell-card` + hover), and quality badges (`.quality-badge` with color-specific dark overrides).
- **Dark mode contract**: Consumers are expected to set `darkMode: 'media'`. When adding a class, add its light style in the main map and mirror the dark adjustments in the existing dark block. Maintain color pairings (e.g., gray-200 → gray-700, blue-500 → blue-400, red-50 → red-900).
- **CSS style approach**: Favor `@apply` for Tailwind utilities. Non-utility properties are used sparingly (e.g., `.skeleton` height/width). Keep transitions/animations consistent with existing durations/easings (`duration-700 ease-out` for fades, `duration-500 ease-out` for progress, `transition-all duration-200` for buttons).
- **Caution**: The bottom of [tailwind-ai-preview-plugin.js](../tailwind-ai-preview-plugin.js) currently includes an embedded Tailwind config example that reassigns `module.exports`. If you refactor, ensure the plugin export remains intact (do not lose the plugin function) and keep any example config separated or clearly commented.
- **Installation/usage example**: See [README.md](../README.md) for minimal usage. Typical consumer flow: install, add to `plugins` in `tailwind.config.js`, set `content` globs, and apply classes to preview markup.
- **Release workflow**: Semantic Release runs on pushes to `main` via [.github/workflows/release.yml](workflows/release.yml). Steps: checkout, Node 22 setup, `npm ci`, ad-hoc lint (`npx eslint . --ext .js`), then `npx semantic-release`.
- **Versioning**: Conventional commits drive version bumps. `release.config.js` extends semantic-release defaults and commits changelog + package.json with a `chore(release): ... [skip ci]` message.
- **Publishing**: Publishes to the public npm registry under the scoped name `@premium-ai/preview-ui`. Root [.npmrc](../.npmrc) and [.github/.npmrc](.npmrc) expect `NPM_TOKEN`; GitHub Actions also needs `NPM_TOKEN` and uses the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- **Dependencies**: Only peer dependency is `tailwindcss>=3.0.0`. No runtime deps; dev deps are semantic-release plugins.
- **Local edits/testing**: There is no build step. After edits, you can verify by requiring the plugin in a sample Tailwind config and running Tailwind CLI in a consuming app. Keep API surface minimal—add new classes via `addComponents` rather than altering public shape.
- **Linting**: CI installs eslint on-the-fly; no repo-level config is present. If adding lint rules, include configuration files or pin eslint to avoid CI surprises.
- **Docs/changelog**: Update [README.md](../README.md) when introducing new component classes or usage patterns. Changelog is auto-managed by semantic-release; do not hand-edit unless adjusting historical notes.
- **Safety**: Avoid adding non-ASCII unless necessary. Preserve semantic-release workflow expectations (main branch only). Do not remove `.npmrc` files—they are required for publishing.
